content.title: Affordable Housing in Arvada
content.summary: Arvada, Colorado, is addressing a housing affordability crisis exacerbated by demographic and socioeconomic shifts, as highlighted in its 2024 Housing Strategic Plan. The city is implementing various strategies, including opting into Proposition 123 for funding, establishing a Housing Advisory Committee, and managing Community Development Block Grants to support affordable housing initiatives. Additionally, the Arvada Housing Authority administers Housing Choice Vouchers and participates in partnerships to promote income-restricted housing projects.
content.body:
## Introduction

Arvada is the seventh largest city in the State of Colorado and is part of the Denver Metro Area and the Front Range Urban Corridor. Like many communities in Colorado, Arvada has been hit hard by the national housing shortage and affordability crisis. Once a farming and industrial community, Arvada is now facing demographic, socioeconomic and affordability shifts.

To adapt to these challenges, the City is using many tools and strategies to help stabilize and diversify its housing stock and address the dynamic needs of its current and future residents. A new assessment was completed in 2024. Based on those findings, the Arvada City Council adopted the Arvada Housing Strategic Plan.

[HOUSING NEEDS ASSESSMENT](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1276/2023-Housing-Assessment-Findings)

[HOUSING STRATEGIC PLAN](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1277/2024-Housing-Strategic-Plan)

## City's Current Role in Promoting and Preserving Affordability

### Housing Division

The Arvada Housing Division is currently working to improve housing affordability in Arvada in six key ways:

1. **Strategic Plan:**The Arvada Housing Division recently released the Arvada Housing Strategic Plan, which included a 2023 Housing Assessment. The findings of the assessment were incorporated into the strategies recommended for adoption by the plan.
2. **Opting In to Proposition 123:** In July 2023, the City of Arvada opted in to Proposition 123 for the 2024-2026 funding cycle. This allows affordable housing developers and service providers who operate within the City to apply for funding from the grant.
3. **Housing Advisory Committee:** The Housing Advisory Committee is a resident committee that meets quarterly to discuss and promote housing opportunities and strategies in the City. This committee provided ongoing feedback as the Arvada Strategic Housing Plan was written and will be instrumental in determining how the City moves forward with the plan.
4. **Grant application support:** The City works with private entities to apply for grant financing that is only accessible to municipalities or nonprofit organizations. The City employs a full-time Housing Grant Administrator who can work with them to apply for grant financing on their behalf.
5. **Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) distribution and management:** Arvada is given its own allocation of CDBG funds annually. The Housing Division manages and administers these funds and competitively awards them to projects and initiatives in the City.
6. **HOME Consortium:** In 2024, Arvada joined the Jefferson County HOME Consortium and will be eligible to receive HOME Funds.

### Arvada Housing Authority

The [Arvada Housing Authority](/435/Arvada-Housing-Authority) has several tools to help promote and improve affordability.

1. [**Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8):**](/438/Arvada-Housing-Authority---Housing-Choic) The Arvada Housing Authority administers 562 Housing Choice Vouchers which can be used to supplement rent for low-income households in Arvada. These have been used to keep at-risk families housed and get homeless families into housing.
2. [**Project-Based Vouchers:**](/952/Project-Based-Voucher-Program) The Project-Based Voucher Program allows Public Housing Authorities to attach up to 20% of their total voucher allocation to units. The Arvada Housing Authority has been using this to support income-restricted housing projects and has awarded vouchers to multiple projects in Arvada.
3. **Special Limited Partnerships:** The Arvada Housing Authority, through its wholly owned affiliate, Arvada Housing Participation, LP., participates in the ownership entities of several affordable and income-restricted properties in the City. This participation exempts the property from a use tax during construction, and annual state and local taxes.
4. **Arvada Affordable Housing Fund:** The Arvada Housing Authority manages a fund to provide gap financing loans to upcoming construction projects in Arvada. The criteria for the Fund is revised annually by the Housing Advisory Committee.

1. [Arvada Affordable Housing Fund: Resource for Developers](#tabbdbe8a52-06a0-4c74-b7a6-246b9581c90b_0)

The Arvada Affordable Housing Fund is a gap financing source available to housing developers looking to build and rehabilitate projects in Arvada. Funds are released annually or biannually, depending on the operating levels, through a competitive process. Priority and threshold criteria for each cycle are determined by the Housing Advisory Committee, in alignment with the City’s short-term affordable housing goals.

1. [Affordable Housing Inventory (Income-Restricted)](#tabbdbe8a52-06a0-4c74-b7a6-246b9581c90b_1)

The City of Arvada currently has 23 affordable properties in its total housing stock. These units were built using Federal, State and Local money, and are under income restrictions as a condition of accepting these funds. The City does not own or manage these properties, but offers support and partnership where appropriate. Read more on the [Affordable Housing Inventory webpage](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1339/Affordable-Housing-Inventory).

## Upcoming Affordable and WorkForce Housing Projects

- **Marshall Street Landing:** 85 units, all Vouchers, Permanent Supportive Housing for formerly homeless persons
- **Legacy Senior Residences:**72 Units, LIHTC, 62+ Senior Housing
- **Marshall Pointe:**260 Units, LIHTC
- **Habitat for Humanity Townhomes:**20 Units, Affordable Homeownership, 80% AMI income-limit.

## City of Arvada Lawsuit and Affordable Housing

The City of Arvada will join five other cities in the Denver metropolitan area in suing the State of Colorado in an effort to defend local municipalities' rights to Home Rule on matters of land use and development.

Arvada is committed to increasing access to affordable housing, and already encourages higher density in appropriate areas while respecting the character of local neighborhoods and the desires of residents. The City welcomes and encourages affordable housing in Arvada by considering reduced parking, additional building height, and participating as a partner in affordable housing projects. The Colorado Constitution gives Arvada the authority to implement affordable housing strategies in a way that is best for our unique jurisdiction based on input from Arvada residents. This authority is what Arvada is attempting to preserve through the lawsuit. [Read more about the lawsuit in the FAQs](https://www.arvadaco.gov/Faq.aspx?TID=100).
